t: The battle was the largest naval battle and the only full-scale clash of battleships of the First World War, and the last major naval battle in any war fought primarily by battleships.
The British lost 14 ships and the Germans 11, and the British lost more sailors, yet the High Seas Fleet never again sought a fleet action, and the British blockade of Germany continued.
Both sides claimed victory, and there is no consensus over which nation was victorious, or whether there was a victor at all.
dyk: A copy of the main German codebook, taken from the light cruiser SMS Magdeburg after she ran aground in Russian waters in 1914, meant the British Admiralty could often read German naval signals, and it knew a major German operation was likely before Scheer sailed.
ev: Scheer replaces the ill Admiral von Pohl as commander of the German fleet
The German Admiralty halts indiscriminate submarine attacks on merchant shipping after neutral protests
Jellicoe sails from Scapa Flow on 30 May after the Admiralty intercepts Scheer's signal
Beatty and Hipper meet on 31 May; Indefatigable and Queen Mary are lost in the battlecruiser action
Jellicoe deploys at 18:15, and the main fleets engage twice before dark
Scheer breaks through the British rear in the night and the German fleet reaches port
A German advance into the North Sea is nearly intercepted by the Grand Fleet
The United States declares war on Germany after unrestricted submarine warfare resumes

f.date: 31 May to 1 June 1916, in extensive manoeuvring and three main engagements
f.place: The North Sea off the coast of Denmark's Jutland Peninsula, near the mouth of the Skagerrak
f.sides: The Royal Navy's Grand Fleet under Admiral Sir John Jellicoe, with Vice-Admiral Sir David Beatty commanding its battlecruisers, against the Imperial German Navy's High Seas Fleet under Vice-Admiral Reinhard Scheer, with Vice-Admiral Franz Hipper commanding its scouting force; the two fleets totalled 250 ships
f.outcome: Fourteen British and eleven German ships sank, with 9,823 dead in all. The Germans broke through the British rear in the night and returned to port; both sides claimed victory, and there is no consensus on which nation won, or whether either did.
